values.note: Counts differ by page: BLM's accessibility survey (uploaded April 2026) gives 2 camping loops with 19 campsites, each for 2 vehicles, packed-gravel spurs (concrete at accessible site 16); BLM's description says 17 designated camping spurs, 10 with shade structures; the FS page says 22. Also a separate, more dispersed equestrian camping loop. No length stated.

sites.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/bradfield-recreation-site ('North of the day-use area are 2 camping loops with a total of 19 campsites, each of which accommodates 2 vehicles'; 'Descriptions and photos uploaded April 2026'; 'There are 17 designated camping spurs with picnic tables and fire rings. Ten of the sites have shade structures'; 'an additional camping loop geared toward more dispersed camping for equestrian users') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/sanjuan/recreation/bradfield-campground ('large and open with 22 campsites'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Two double-vault toilets. Potable water from hand pumps, seasonal (BLM: generally April 1 - Sept 30; its accessibility survey says March through Sept 30); the FS page says September-May brings limited or no services (water, trash, restrooms). Boat ramp and trailer parking; day-use area with shade shelters. No cell coverage.

facilities.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/bradfield-recreation-site ('two vault restrooms and two potable water hand pumps (seasonally operational, generally April 1st -Sept 30th)'; 'Potable water is available from 1 spigot, operated by a hand pump, from March through September 30 each year'; 'There is no cell phone coverage at this site.') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/sanjuan/recreation/bradfield-campground ('Between September and May, there are limited or no services (water, trash pick up or restrooms)'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: First come, first served; pay at the kiosk's fee tube.

booking.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/bradfield-recreation-site ('There is an $8/night camping fee on a first come first served basis'; 'Stay Limit: 14 Day Stay Limit'; 'A kiosk with site and safety information and a fee-payment tube') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/sanjuan/recreation/bradfield-campground ('All sites are first-come, first serve.'), read 2026-10-28

fees.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/bradfield-recreation-site ('Fees: Day-use picnicking is free. Camping: $8/night.'), read 2026-10-28

note: BLM (Tres Rios Field Office) site in the Dolores River canyon below McPhee Dam, ~30 mi NW of Dolores: US-491 north, then a rough but passable gravel road (FR 505 / CR S) down into the canyon past the Bradfield Bridge. Large, open, flat gravel loops with shade shelters beside the brushy riverbank. Busiest during the lower Dolores boatable release (BLM: generally mid-April to mid-June). --Claude
